record.paper_title: Open Problems in Applying Random-Matrix Theory to Nuclear Reactions
record.context_brief: GOE consistency with compound-nucleus resonance data
record.original_question: Are the statistical properties predicted by the time-reversal-invariant Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (GOE) consistent with experimental data on compound-nucleus resonances strongly enough to justify using random-matrix theory as a physically meaningful tool in nuclear reaction theory, including tests based on resonance spacings, widths, and quantum-number-clean resonance sequences?

evidence.quote: The question has two parts. (i) Are the properties predicted by the GOE consistent with experimental data on CN resonances? (ii) Is it possible to implement the GOE into a viable and useful theory of nuclear resonance reactions? An affirmative answer to question (i) is the neccessary condition for a physically meaningful use of RMT in nuclear reaction theory.
In general, the data agree with GOE predictions. Open questions exist for the ∆3 statistic for long sequences of levels, and for the distribution of neutron widths.

artifact.status_search_result: Spacing statistics and short-range fluctuations of compound-nucleus resonance sequences agree well with GOE predictions, providing strong empirical support for random-matrix theory in nuclear reaction theory. However, two issues flagged as open remain actively debated: the Δ_3 spectral rigidity for long sequences, and the distribution of reduced neutron widths. Reanalyses of the nuclear data ensemble (e.g., Koehler et al.) reported significant deviations from the Porter-Thomas distribution, and subsequent works have proposed mechanisms (non-statistical γ decay, continuum coupling, channel coupling breaking orthogonal invariance) that produce such deviations. Recent experimental work (e.g., 150Nd, 2025) continues to find departures from ν=1 chi-squared behavior. The overall question is therefore partially resolved: GOE is broadly consistent with most observables but tensions persist for neutron-width statistics and long-range rigidity.

status_evidence.title: Neutron Resonance Widths and the Porter-Thomas Distribution
status_evidence.snippet: Reanalyses of the nuclear data ensemble revealed significant deviations from PT predictions.
status_evidence.claim: Reduced neutron width distributions deviate from the GOE-predicted Porter-Thomas form.

status_evidence.title: Deviations from the Porter-Thomas Distribution due to Nonstatistical γ Decay below the 150Nd Neutron Separation Threshold
status_evidence.snippet: An average branching ratio is related to a degree of freedom of ν=1.93(12), rejecting the validity of the Porter-Thomas distribution.
status_evidence.claim: Recent experiments find deviations from the Porter-Thomas (ν=1) distribution attributable to non-statistical decay.

status_evidence.title: Neutron width statistics in a realistic resonance-reaction model
status_evidence.snippet: Channel coupling produces an effective Hamiltonian with a GOE term plus a coupling term with broken orthogonal symmetry, modifying width distributions.
status_evidence.claim: Channel coupling provides a mechanism for deviations from GOE/Porter-Thomas predictions.
